t: This is the Cobden Club, a Victorian society and publishing imprint that never had permanent premises of its own. It was run like a gentlemen's club, for people who believed in free trade. Thomas Bayley Potter, a Manchester merchant and Liberal politician, founded it in 1866 and served as its honorary secretary until his death in 1898. It is named for Richard Cobden, who died the year before. Cobden was a Radical and Liberal politician and manufacturer who campaigned for free trade and peace.
